evals.name: author-from-scratch-power-led
evals.prompt: I'm writing a markdown design doc for a tiny prototype board and I need a tscircuit code block I can drop in. The block should show a 3.3V rail driving a single red status LED through a 1k current-limiting resistor to ground. Just the schematic — I don't care about PCB placement. Keep it minimal and make sure the LED actually shows as connected when rendered.

assertions.text: TSX output file exists and is non-empty
Trace selectors use the canonical `.X > .pin` form (no plain `.X .pin` space-without-`>` form, which is the bug pattern)
Lets auto-layout do the work — no `schAutoLayoutEnabled={false}` and no manual `schX/schY` props (per skill Rule 3)
Render produces at least one schematic_trace (the R↔LED inter-component wire)
Rendered PNG is at least 5 KB (a near-empty schematic is tiny)

evals.name: debug-broken-button-circuit
evals.prompt: Fix a tscircuit code block where the pushbutton is floating and the MOSFET doesn't draw. The original had `.X .pin` selectors, `.side1/.side2` on the pushbutton, and a missing `mosfetMode`.

assertions.text: Output TSX has zero `.X .pinN` selectors (the broken form) — only `.X > .pinN`
Output TSX has zero references to `.side1` or `.side2` (uses `.pin1`/`.pin2` for pushbutton)
Output TSX sets `mosfetMode=` on every `<mosfet>` element
Render produces no `source_pin_missing_trace_warning` for pin1/pin2 (the authored pins). Pin3/pin4 warnings on pushbutton are benign — bridged-pole pins don't need separate connections
Render produces all four components (R_PU, SW1, C_DB, Q1) as schematic_components

evals.name: multi-channel-can-bus-array
evals.prompt: Author a 4-channel CAN-FD transceiver array with custom-pinLabel chips, 120Ω terminations, shared VCC_5V/GND, per-channel CANx_TX/CANx_RX nets.

assertions.text: Each chip declares pinLabels including TXD, RXD, VDD, VSS, CANH, CANL
Output TSX declares 4 termination resistors with `resistance="120"` (or equivalent)
Output TSX references `net.VCC_5V` and `net.GND` from every chip
Output TSX references the 8 per-channel nets CAN0_TX/CAN0_RX through CAN3_TX/CAN3_RX
